learning_outcomes.text: Students must demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the basic issues related to active microwave remote sensing, the main electromagnetic scattering models from rough surfaces, and the basic concepts of SAR data processing. The educational path aims to provide students with basic knowledge and methodological tools to analyze active remote sensing systems and interpret microwave remote sensing data.
Students must demonstrate the ability to use the acquired knowledge by applying it concretely to the analysis of simple active remote sensing systems and the processing of SAR remote sensing data.

syllabus_topics: Real Aperture Radar: chirp signals and their processing, spatial resolutions.

Synthetic Aperture Radar: spatial and radiometric resolutions, focusing and data processing. Geometric distortions of remote sensing data, creation of data for geographic information systems. Electromagnetic models for fading and speckle, multilook techniques.
Radar Interferometry: principles and data processing schemes; causes and decorrelation models. Differential interferometry.

Main electromagnetic scattering models and their interpretation: geometric and electromagnetic models of random surfaces; Kirchhoff approximation, Physical Optics and Geometric Optics solutions for deterministic and random rough surfaces, limits of validity. Models for sea surfaces. Electromagnetic scattering from sea surfaces.
Altimeters: operating principles, applications for sea and ice studies.
Scatterometers: operating principles, applications to land and sea, wind estimation.

Satellite remote sensing of the terrestrial environment: applications to soil, sea, ice, urban areas. Remote sensing for interplanetary explorations. Integration of remote sensing data. Analysis of remote sensing data from space agencies: ASI, ESA, NASA. Missions: ERS, ENVISAT, SIR, CASSINI.

Processing of remote sensing data. Use of the virtual laboratory provided by the European Space Agency (ESA) consisting of high-capacity and high-speed virtual computers, ESA software from the SNAP category, SAR data from the ESA Open Hub. All can be operated by students directly on their own PCs. The main activities concern: image visualization, speckle filtering, interferometry, marine SAR applications, processing and visualization of multi-temporal SAR data. The data processing leads to a report that can be discussed during the exam.

assessment_methods.method: Discussion of a project report (optional based on data processing activity)

assessment_rules: The exam consists solely of an oral examination. The processing of remote sensing data leads to a report that can be discussed during the exam.
